submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, bugs_open/474 — found on the first run of delivery-review-filer ever, during the owner-authorised delivery rehearsal.
rationale:
ROUND 2, acting on all of round 1's REVISE. Two objections found a real design flaw in what 751 shipped, two found robustness gaps, and one is a process criticism I accept without argument.

THE DESIGN FLAW (guardian, medium + low). 751 set `spec_paths.review_data = 'input_data'`, pointing the key at the whole map the filer happens to be handed. That is unconstrained: it copies whatever else input_data carries — orchestration bookkeeping, envelope fields, anything a future step adds — verbatim into `spec.review_data`, which the admin screen renders DIRECTLY to the owner. A future unrelated change to this agent's input_data would silently change what he is shown, with nothing reviewing that coupling. The low objection is the sharper statement of it: 751's backfill of the already-filed row built {domain, site_url, brief} from that row's own spec, while its config change gives every FUTURE row {site_id, domain, site_url, brief}. ONE FIELD, TWO SHAPES, diverging silently at the boundary between the patched item and the next one. I introduced that divergence and did not see it.

THE FIX IS THE SHAPE I REJECTED WHEN WRITING 751. `spec_paths.review_data = 'input_data.review_data'`: the dispatcher composes the object explicitly as exactly {domain, site_url, brief} — the same three fields 751 backfilled, so the two shapes become one. I rejected it on the grounds that it 'moves work onto every future caller to fix a defect none of them caused'. The objections change that balance, and the cost turns out to be the POINT: create_work_item treats an unresolved spec_path as a HARD ERROR (create_work_item_action.go:287-296, 'refusing to create a work item with an incomplete spec'), so a dispatcher that forgets gets a loud refusal AT DISPATCH, in front of the operator who just ran it — instead of silently filing an item the owner cannot approve and will not understand. Trading a silent dead-end for a loud failure is the trade this bug exists to make. The RUNBOOK recipe is the only caller today and ships updated in the same commit.

THE TWO ROBUSTNESS GAPS, both real, both now closed BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by verify. (editquality, high) jsonb_set with create_missing=false returns the document UNCHANGED when the path is absent — a silent no-op reporting success. 751 survived only because its DO/RAISE verify would have caught it after the fact; 752's anchor guard asserts spec_paths EXISTS and is an object BEFORE the write. (debug_historian, medium) jsonb || NULL is NULL, so concatenating onto an absent spec_paths would WIPE it rather than add a key — COALESCE closes that. Both are the same family as a hazard I found in my own 466 change earlier the same day, which makes missing them here less forgivable, not more.

THE PROCESS OBJECTION (debug_historian, high), accepted without argument. 751 was APPLIED BY HAND BEFORE the council saw it, so the seats audited a change already live. That is accurate. The reason was that the owner was blocked on an unapprovable review item and the fix was one config key; the mitigation was a snapshot, an anchor guard, a DO/RAISE verify and a committed ROLLBACK file — none of which the submission listed as an edit, so the seats could not see any of it and judged a bare jsonb_set, which is all I gave them. 752 IS SUBMITTED BEFORE IT IS APPLIED, and its rollback is a listed edit rather than a claim in prose.

WHAT I AM NOT CHANGING, and why. bug_historian raised bugs_closed/054 (an input_data authored as a full message envelope double-wraps, so the payload lands one level too deep). Answered empirically rather than by reading: the item that WAS filed resolved input_data.brief, input_data.domain and input_data.site_url — all three present in its spec — so input_data is single-wrapped on this dispatch path. 752 adds one more segment to a path shape already proven to resolve here.

Forward-only: 751 stands in history and its backfill was correct. 752 narrows the config to match it.

plan.summary: Narrow delivery-review-filer's `review_data` from 'the whole input_data map' to an object the DISPATCHER composes (domain, site_url, brief) — one shape for the backfilled item and every future one, no unreviewed coupling to whatever input_data grows, and a LOUD refusal at file time if a caller omits it. Plus the two write-safety gaps the round found, closed by construction.

edits.rationale: Supersedes 751's shape. The anchor guard asserts spec_paths EXISTS and is an object before writing (editquality's silent no-op) and that review_data currently holds 751's value. The concatenation is COALESCE-guarded (debug_historian's jsonb||NULL wipe). The verify asserts the new value, that the three sibling keys survived the ||, that checkpoint:true is undisturbed, AND that the already-filed item carries exactly the 3 fields the dispatcher now composes — it asserts the CONVERGENCE of the two shapes rather than assuming it.
edits.sketch:
IF sp IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(sp) <> 'object' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '…jsonb_set would no-op silently'; END IF;
IF sp->>'review_data' IS DISTINCT FROM 'input_data' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '…751 not applied, or already superseded'; END IF;
jsonb_set(default_config,'{workflow,steps,file_review,config,spec_paths}',
  COALESCE(…->'spec_paths','{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('review_data','input_data.review_data'), false)
-- verify additionally asserts convergence:
IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='needs_delivery_review'
           AND (SELECT count(*) FROM jsonb_object_keys(spec->'review_data')) <> 3) THEN RAISE …

edits.rationale: Listed as an edit this time, which is exactly what round 1's submission failed to do — the seats objected to a bare jsonb_set because a bare jsonb_set is all they were shown. Guarded both ways: refuses unless review_data currently holds 752's value, and its verify asserts the sibling keys survived. It restores a shape the round found worse but which is not broken, so it is safe to run.
edits.sketch:
IF sp->>'review_data' IS DISTINCT FROM 'input_data.review_data' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '…nothing to roll back'; END IF;
COALESCE(…,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('review_data','input_data')
